New Motivation:
While higher total daily energy intake can lead to increases in average body size (BMI) within a population, the socio-cultural ideal BMI is shaped by a complex interplay of factors including media representation, cultural values, historical trends, and economic influences, alongside prevailing average body sizes. Although larger average body sizes might, over time, influence cultural perceptions and desirability norms, this relationship is indirect and moderated by many confounding variables and does not follow deterministically from energy intake alone.
